clue.text: Farming crops using new soil, accept visual aids in lab may be this

definitions.text: visual aids in lab may be this

indicators.note: farming works and turns over the ground, so the letters that follow are worked into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Agricultural advice about tilling crops in fresh soil, oddly ending up in a science lab.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Farming' signals the anagram; 'using new' and the comma are link padding for the surface. CROPS, SOIL and ACCEPT together supply all fifteen letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Instruments that split light into a spectrum are optical aids, and anything relating to them is described by this adjective.

clue.text: Take me for a pain and call it a day (sic) — I cycle all over the place

indicators.note: something all over the place is scattered in disorder, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A cyclist gives up for the day, the bracketed sic noting the odd phrasing, as they ride erratically.
explanation.walkthrough: The parenthetical (sic) looks like an editor's note but its three letters are part of the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the chemical name of aspirin, the tablet one takes to relieve a headache or other pain.

clue.text: Mary would have taken issue with this!

definitions.text: Mary would have taken issue with this!

parts.words: Mary would have taken issue with this!
parts.note: issue means offspring: the Virgin Mary conceived her child, Jesus, in the Catholic doctrine of being free from original sin; on the surface Mary disagrees

explanation.surface: Someone called Mary would have objected to something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Taken issue with' means disagreed with on the surface; cryptically 'issue' is a child, so Mary came to have her child through it.
explanation.definitionFit: Christian doctrine holds that Mary herself was conceived free of original sin, the dogma known by this name.

clue.text: Current Hindu god, appropriately on feet?

parts.note: Indra is the Vedic god of rain and thunder

explanation.surface: A question whether an air current suits a Hindu deity standing on his feet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'appropriately on' are link words; in a down clue the god sits on top of the feet.
explanation.definitionFit: An indraft is an inward flow of air or water, a kind of current.

clue.text: A best-seller, he devastates saloons with abandon

indicators.note: acting with abandon means wildly and without restraint, so the letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: A rampaging man wrecks bars, as in the old joke about a gun-toting panda.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface retells the punctuation joke behind Lynne Truss's best-selling grammar book: a panda eats, fires a gun and walks out of a bar.
explanation.definitionFit: Lynne Truss's 2003 book on punctuation sold in millions, making it a best-seller.

clue.text: See 5
Net redesigned as it's stopped in the last month dual crime

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: stopped means plugged, so the two outer pieces enclose the middle group

parts.note: read two ways: December is the last month of the year, abbreviated Dec
read the second way: ult. (ultimo) means of last month in old business letters

indicators.note: something redesigned is put together in a new form, so these letters are reordered

parts.note: taken as written
it is crossword slang for sex appeal, SA

explanation.surface: A rearranged net has been blocked in a double crime last month.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dual' says 'the last month' is read twice, as December and as ultimo; 'stopped' puts the anagram from 'redesigned' and the rest between them. 'it' as sex appeal is dated crossword slang.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a criminal offence of unwanted sexual touching, so it names a crime.

clue.text: Traveller in suit came meandering across bridge

indicators.note: the bridge stretches across the jumbled letters, holding them inside

parts.note: a span is a bridge or the part between its supports

indicators.note: meandering wanders about, so the letters of the word wander into a new order

explanation.surface: A traveller in a suit wanders over a bridge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'meandering' scrambles the verb into ACEM; 'across' has the bridge spanning it. 'Traveller in suit' suggests a businessman, but the suit is a spacesuit.
explanation.definitionFit: An astronaut travels through space wearing a pressurised suit.

clue.text: The solution is around the city

indicators.note: the solution word goes round the other piece, enclosing it

parts.note: ans. is a short form of answer, a solution

explanation.surface: The answer to a puzzle surrounds a city.
explanation.definitionFit: Athens is the capital city of Greece.

clue.text: Is coat tailored up north?

indicators.note: tailored cloth is cut and refashioned, so these letters are refashioned

explanation.surface: A question about whether a coat was made by a tailor in the north.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up north' looks like an adverb describing where the coat is tailored; it is the definition, a place name.
explanation.definitionFit: Scotia is the Latin or poetic name for Scotland, the land up north of England.

clue.text: Put back dodgy stereo in a small way

indicators.note: one piece sits inside the abbreviation for the way

parts.note: Rd is the short form of road, a way

indicators.note: dodgy means unreliable or faulty, so the letters of stereo are rearranged

explanation.surface: Returning a faulty stereo bit by bit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dodgy' rearranges the hi-fi into ESTORE; 'in a small way' looks like 'slightly' but is the road abbreviation holding it.
explanation.definitionFit: Something restored has been put back in place or returned to a former condition.

clue.text: Piece of Beethoven has gone, gone from the mouth

indicators.note: has gone means is no longer there, so the next piece is taken out

parts.note: the Pastoral is the popular name of Beethoven's Sixth Symphony
gone means past, over and done

explanation.surface: A Beethoven work is over and done with, no longer heard from anyone's lips.
explanation.walkthrough: Beethoven's Sixth Symphony is subtitled Pastoral; removing PAST leaves the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Oral describes what is spoken or comes out of the mouth, as in an oral examination.

clue.text: Cryptic confused us with lack of definition

indicators.note: cryptic means puzzling or obscure, so these letters are rearranged in a puzzling way

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A cryptic clue baffles us by being vague.
explanation.walkthrough: 'confused' looks like the anagram signal, but it is fodder; 'Cryptic' is the indicator.
explanation.definitionFit: An image or idea lacking sharpness is blurred, without definition.

clue.text: See 3
A long story is over about weapon

indicators.note: the turned word goes round the story, enclosing it
over means turned upside down, so the word is reversed in this down-free across reading

parts.note: a saga is a long story

explanation.surface: A long story finishes concerning a weapon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' turns the little word into SI; 'is over' reads like 'has ended' in the surface. Assagai is also spelt assegai.
explanation.definitionFit: An assagai is a slender spear used in southern Africa, a weapon.

clue.text: Suffering vocal change in one that's senseless!

indicators.note: suffering means undergoing, and vocal is read as vowel: one vowel is swapped for another

parts.note: in one means united, in unity

explanation.surface: Someone undergoes a change of voice, yet seems senseless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'vocal change' means a vowel change: the U in IN UNITY becomes an A.
explanation.definitionFit: Inanity is silliness, and an inanity is a foolish remark, something lacking sense.

clue.text: Artisan left master in northeast town

indicators.note: the pair sits inside the town word

parts.note: toon is the Geordie word for town, used in northeast England for Newcastle
MA is Master of Arts

explanation.surface: A craftsman left his master in a northeastern town.
explanation.walkthrough: TOON is how Newcastle people in northeast England say 'town'.
explanation.definitionFit: A toolman is a worker skilled with tools, a craftsman or artisan.

clue.text: Caravan phone-in?

parts.note: a mobile is a mobile phone
being in means being at home

explanation.surface: A radio phone-in programme about caravans.
explanation.definitionFit: A large caravan used as a permanent dwelling is called by this name.

clue.text: Most unlikely model to endure weight

definitions.meaning: the least likely, as in the final person to do something
a cobbler's wooden foot shape for making shoes
an old measure of weight or quantity, as of gunpowder

explanation.surface: The model least likely to carry weight.
explanation.walkthrough: Four definitions: least likely, a shoemaker's model, endure, and an old unit of weight.
explanation.definitionFit: The word carries all four senses: final, shoemaker's form, persist, and an old unit of load.

clue.text: Here mayor's found it — the young can stay here initially in ring

indicators.note: the two pieces go inside the ring word

parts.note: to ring is to call on the phone
taken as written

parts.words: the young can stay here initially
parts.note: a youth hostel is where the young can stay; its initials are YH

explanation.surface: A mayor found it, a place for young people to stay, in a ring.
explanation.walkthrough: YH comes from Youth Hostel, the place 'the young can stay', reduced to initials.
explanation.definitionFit: The building housing a city's government is where its mayor has an office.

clue.text: See 2
Heading for Jordan's capital? No mass and no exception

parts.note: heading for means going to

indicators.note: no means without, so the letter for mass is dropped

parts.note: Amman is the capital of Jordan
m is the symbol for mass in physics

explanation.surface: Travelling to the Jordanian capital, with no Mass to attend and no exceptions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'No mass' reads as a church service; it is the physics symbol m, dropped from the Jordanian capital.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means every one without exception, as in 'they agreed to a man'.

clue.text: Society's most important member?

parts.note: Society is the Society Islands of French Polynesia; their largest and principal island

explanation.surface: Who is the leading figure in a social club?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Society' looks like a social circle, but it is the Society Islands in the Pacific.
explanation.definitionFit: Tahiti is the largest island of the Society Islands, so their chief member.

clue.text: Most importantly, a lovable bust

indicators.note: bust means broken, so the letters are broken up and rearranged

explanation.surface: Above all, a lovable sculpted bust.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bust' looks like a sculpture or chest; it signals an anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is used to single out the most important point, more than anything else.
